newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IWP says strong punt hits Dutch earnings.
newsitem.headline: IWP says strong punt hits Dutch earnings.

text.p: Ireland's industrial holding group IWP International Plc said on Thursday that it was confident of achieving continuing growth in the current year but added that currency fluctuations were having an adverse effect on its Dutch earnings.

IWP said in a results statement that its half-year pre-tax profit was up 10 percent to 9.64 million punts and that both its household/personal care and labels/distribution divisions were currently trading satisfactorily and ahead of last year.
The company said the current strength of the Irish pound against the Dutch guilder was having an adverse impact on the translation of Dutch earnings.
"If the trend continues Dutch profits this year could be over one million (Irish) pounds less on translation than if last year's exchange rate had prevailed," the statement said.
IWP said the performance over the six months had been very satisfactory with sales, profits and earnings per share showing strong growth over the relevant 1995 figures.
It said turnover had increased by 17 percent to 87.10 million punts while operating profit had risen to 10.74 million punts from 9.68 million punts previously.

The company said this had been achieved despite an adverse currency translation of over 400,000 Irish pounds as a result of the strengthening Irish punt agains the Dutch guilder when compared with last year's exchange rate.

IWP said, as predicted, its gearing ratio had increased due to the purchase of the preference shares relating to Royal Sanders, a subsidiary of Levendaal Beheer BV, independent manufacturer of persoanl care and household products in the Netherlands, which it purchased in 1993.
The company said interest cover at almost 10 times underlined its strong financial position and cash generation.
IWP said its household and personal care division, which was now the core of the Group, had continued to grow in terms of both turnover and profit.
But within the division, the company said, Burlington results were below expectation. IWP bought Burlington Holdings Ltd. in December 1995.
"This company's sales had frown rapidly over the last three years but the management structures, necessary to underpin future growth, were less than our standards.," IWP said.

"In view of this we significantly increased investment in management and infrastructure which we are confident will give good returns in the future but will result in little or no growth in Burlington in the current year," it added.
IWP said the performance of its labels/distribution division had been most satisfactory and though small relative to its core division is an important contributor to overall profits.
IWP said the purchase of the Polish company, Polbita, a company engaged in the sale and distribution of household and personal care products, was a significant growth market.

The company said margins were and continued to be small and its aim over a number of years was to improve these by better selling prices and reduced costs. --Damien Lynch, Dublin Newsroom +353 1 676 9775
